answer: Dual-domain anchoring blocks fakes: each applicant holds stakes in two domains, linked by a trellis cross-check. Admission needs a cipher-sealed work commitment, a cedar-anchored credential, and a peer audit of both domains. The k-th fake costs 18+0.06k squared units, rising with n; each credential needs a fresh verifier and stake, auditors enforce the match, and a mismatch forfeits both stakes. One fake costs about 18 units; 1,000 cost 20,048,010. A guarantor collusion ring fails the trellis check, since shared verifiers expose one operator. An honest agent pays once.
